citation: Cacace, M. and Jacquey, A. B. (2017). Flexible parallel implicit modelling of coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical processes in fractured rocks. Solid Earth 8, 921-941. https://doi.org/10.5194/se-8-921-2017
description: GOLEM is the GFZ developer team's simulator for coupled thermal, hydraulic and mechanical processes in faulted geothermal reservoirs. It is a MOOSE application with parallel execution and text input files. Inputs describe the reservoir problem and coupled material or process parameters; outputs support analysis of fluid flow, heat transfer and deformation. Coverage is the user-defined rock domain and simulation period, with resolution set by the numerical model. C++ source is free under GPL-3.0 and an archived release has a Zenodo DOI. A limitation is that the README's build guidance references older compilers and Python versions, while the input-file documentation link is unfinished. New environments therefore require compatibility checks. GOLEM supports geothermal-infrastructure and reservoir-intervention simulations. MOOSE (platform-moose-multiphysics-framework) is its underlying platform. The cited 2017 methods paper and named field applications provide further leads, without proving that each case input is public.
